newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks firmer, most seen stagnating.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks firmer, most seen stagnating.

text.p: Croatian stocks firmed in lively trade on Tuesday but traders cast doubts on chances of share prices moving up significantly before local elections, set for April 13.
"This is a typical pre-election month stagnation," said Marko Nikolac of Metroholding brokerage, adding that slower buying might cause some stocks to dip.
He singled out blue chip Zagrebacka Banka as seeing a trade increase and even a slight rise.
"There is a positive wind about Zagrebacka, expecting to get a credit rating in some three weeks from now," said Nikolac.
Zagrebacka's ordinary shares rose 30 kuna to 1,900 with 4,143 units changing hands, making it the most active stock.
Another bank stock Dalmatinska, which has risen steadily since the market got wind of its planned candidacy for a full listing, was expected to come off its recent highs.
Dalmatinska Banka led decliners, losing 35 kuna or 8.2 percent to 460 kuna on volume of 115 units.
Seven of fifteen active issues rose, three were flat and five fell. Share volume rose slightly to 12,877 with turnover at 11.1 million kuna.
Another blue chip, drugs firm Pliva was the second most actively traded stock, selling 3,920 units. It closed flat at 470 kuna after a mixed trade.
Textile company Varteks was also heavily traded, selling 1,960 shares in a 70-78 kuna range to close at 75, five higher.
Traders said a recent announcement the company, which has a licence to make Levi Strauss jeans, would be privatised in two months, improved its prospects.
Food concern Podravka, seen as one of the most solid stocks, edged up five kuna to 305 on volume of 855 units.
Five active hoteliers traded mixed on smaller volumes and were seen as likely to slide further, with the exception of Laguna, partly owned by foreign investors.
Suncani Hvar, closing 0.5 kuna lower at 66 kuna, was the most active one with 875 units sold.
The second tranche of public debt refinancing bonds traded flat at 12.14 percent above par on turnover of 2.8 million kuna.
